findings.element: Invoices tab → Invoice date lock note ('To change it, change Schedule start date') and RevRec Schedule start date
findings.finding: The lock note's escape route is a dead end for a user who wants Issued: after switching Schedule start to Invoice issued date and confirming, Invoice date stays locked on Created date with the same note, so RevRec now starts schedules from the issued date while the books still use the created date.
findings.user_impact: A user who follows the note to move to issued dates comes back still locked, with schedules and invoice dates now out of step and no hint that the only unlock is Payment date (which would build schedules from payment dates in the meantime).
findings.suggested_fix: Make Invoice date follow Schedule start while locked (Schedule start = Invoice issued date shows Issued date), or state in the lock note and the confirmation dialog what the Invoice date will be after the change.

evidence.action: Org RevRec · invoice, Invoices tab (Invoice date disabled, 'created', lock note shown) → clicked 'Schedule start date' link → picked Invoice issued date → Change → returned to 1 · Invoices
evidence.observed: Schedule start = 'issued'; Invoice date select still value 'created', disabled=true, lock note unchanged: 'Locked while Revenue Recognition starts schedules from the invoice date. To change it, change Schedule start date.' Dialog body only said 'New schedules will start from the invoice issued date. Existing schedules keep their current dates until they're rebuilt…' and nothing about Invoice date. (State map records only the Payment date unlock; this path was run in the browser.)

findings.element: Summary settings → Sales recording date card
findings.finding: Sales recording date saves the moment it changes, with no confirmation, no success message and no statement of whether existing summaries are re-dated, while its two sibling settings both say the change applies going forward.
findings.user_impact: A user switching Invoice created date → Invoice issued date cannot tell whether it saved or whether past (possibly closed) summary periods will move, so the 'understand what the choice changes' part of the task fails on this screen.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the same going-forward scope the Invoice date description already uses (for example 'Applies to summaries synced from now on') to the Sales recording date description.

evidence.action: Summary settings (existing org) → Sales recording date: picked Payment date, then Invoice issued date
evidence.observed: Value changed to 'payment' then 'issued'; 'Saves on change: no Update button, no confirmation, no success message on this page.' The description reads only 'The date summaries record sales on: when the invoice was created, when it was issued to your customer, or when it was paid. With Payment date there is no Accounts Receivable in summaries.' Invoice date says 'Applies to invoices synced from now on', and the RevRec dialog says 'Existing schedules keep their current dates'.

gaps: Cross-screen Schedule start = Invoice issued date → Invoices lock is not in the state map; it was exercised directly in the browser for UX-1

Reverse mismatch not exercised: Invoice date saved as Issued (while on Payment date), then Schedule start set to Invoice created date. The code suggests the lock would freeze Issued against created-date schedules
Learn more / Upgrade plan links have no destination, so whether the gate's Upgrade path completes is unknown
No save-failure or loading states exist for Update, the Summary save-on-change or the RevRec Change, so error recovery cannot be assessed
Whether live Synder shows a success toast after Update / Summary change / RevRec Change is not recorded, so missing confirmation feedback was only flagged where the scope is also unstated
